scope: Read-only review of all33final training reports and complete33CPU main evaluation files. No checkpoints loaded, rollouts generated, tests/training launched, hyperparameters changed or cycles evaluated.

units.performance: fractions0..1, clean completion on matured primary cohort; ordinary completion separate
units.optimizer_delta: Frobenius norm per actual Adam update
units.gradient: Frobenius norm of normalized pre-clip source mixture
units.trace_gain: homogeneous stage-wise diagonal Heun approximation, not whole-network memory
units.BPTT_horizon: Exact reverse-time graph horizon per source;0 for manual forward-credit modes means no BPTT graph, not zero approximate temporal credit.

interpretation: The symmetric diagonal rule has nonzero task-paired core updates and performs above its actor-shuffled control. This supports the relevance of this signal pairing under this implementation, not exact temporal credit or biological locality.

Persistent and reset64 symmetric traces have similar task results, with no consistent persistent advantage across3seeds. Their homogeneous diagonal64-observation attenuation is approximately2.3e-7 to2.6e-7. E/F can remain nonzero because new sources continually enter; nonzero trace norm is not evidence of long credit.

The instant control retains a history-dependent network state and one current Heun flow sensitivity; it is not a memoryless policy. Its smaller actual recurrent updates and comparable long_sparse scores prevent attributing all local gains to long eligibility history.

Random feedback ends with low global alignment, higher terminal saturation and poor autonomous completion. These are descriptive co-occurrences. There is no matched intervention establishing that saturation, weight growth, alignment or any one factor caused its failure.

Replay improves familiar iid retention for BP and symmetric diagonal credit but changes the objective, old supervision budget and historical BP horizon. The adaptation-retention tradeoff cannot be attributed solely to old-memory use or semantic fusion.

All local/readout arms use external action labels, exact analytic head gradients and inherited BP-pretrained parameters/Adam moments. Forward-only refers to new-phase gradient computation, not the complete training ancestry.

Symmetric local mean realized recurrent Adam delta is0.03241 versus BP64 0.03470 per update, while its head delta is0.02677 versus0.01264. Its poor completion is therefore not explained simply by an orders-of-magnitude smaller realized recurrent update. This comparison does not isolate gradient direction, inherited optimizer effects, learning-rate adequacy or clipping interactions.

Reported parameter deltas are actual realized inherited-Adam increments; raw gradients and joint clipping differ by arm. Larger cumulative or mean delta does not imply better learning, and clipping couples head/core optimization.

Saturation/covariance are one terminal snapshot over heterogeneous actor phases. Pending active/started slot counts are retained to expose state-mixture differences. Centred sample rank cannot exceed63 and is not task representation rank over time or loss-of-plasticity proof.

First-legal accuracy and matched cue-to-legal loss concern the existing head on the learner own states, not all information encoded in h. Never-legal cases are counted separately and cannot be declared forgetting.

The independent Aseed101 tangent audit separately shows that the diagonal projection omits conditional recurrent sensitivity paths. It is not measured on these final33models and does not prove their content-memory mechanism. Exact local sensitivity decay can coexist with discrete memories in distinct attractor basins.

One seed is one statistical replicate. Means and sampleSD use the3seed values. Requests, actors, chunks and independent tangent directions are not extra training replicates. No cycle-v2 result is included here.
